- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast peak at 1.5–2x prior high or add lagged mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model frequently underestimates downward momentum — increase forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- Model consistently underestimates short-term mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast mid-range if sentiment is weakly positive.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., >+0.30), model often overestimates upside — cap forecast at 1.5x prior high or add 0.5% downward adjustment to avoid overhang.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to forecast lower than true — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to offset sentiment-induced pessimism.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lagged mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of history if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
